units.text: ⟦0⟧’s inability to process invalid multibyte characters can be used to detect such invalid sequences in a file. In the following examples, the ⟦1⟧ is an invalid multibyte sequence, while ⟦2⟧ is a valid multibyte sequence (of the Greek Sigma character).

units.text: The following ⟦0⟧ program removes all valid characters using ⟦1⟧. Any content left in the pattern space (the invalid characters) are added to the hold space using the ⟦2⟧ command. On the last line (⟦3⟧), the hold space is retrieved (⟦4⟧), newlines are removed (⟦5⟧), and any remaining octets are printed unambiguously (⟦6⟧). Thus, any invalid multibyte sequences are printed as octal values:
units.sourceHTML: The following sed program removes all valid characters using s/.//g. Any content left in the pattern space (the invalid characters) are added to the hold space using the H command. On the last line ($), the hold space is retrieved (x), newlines are removed (s/\n//g), and any remaining octets are printed unambiguously (l). Thus, any invalid multibyte sequences are printed as octal values:
